text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Denmark's centre-left government is poised to agree to left-wing opposition demands for tighter Danish Iran policies provided they do not participate in any no confidence motion over its clumsy handling of British author Salman Rushdie's visit to Denmark at a parliamentary debate on Thursday.

--- Maersk Line, a unit of Danish shipping group A.P. Moeller, is negotiating with Rotterdam's Europe Combined Terminals (ECT) on establishing its own container terminal at the Dutch port, which is an important centre for the line's traffic with U.S.A. and the Far East.

--- A survey of 76,000 Danish private limited companies shows that telecommunication group Tele Danmark's mobile telephone unit has been the company creating most new jobs with the highest growth in earnings in the past five years. In second place came loudspeaker producer Jamo in western Denmark.

--- A Danish foreign ministry report shows that Denmark's exports to the U.S.A have fallen more than previously assumed compared to other EU countries. This has prompted the ministry and Denmark's Confederation of Industry to initiate new campaigns to create better contact with U.S. companies and encourage more Danish companies to move to the U.S.A.

--- SAS is not prepared for international deregulation and the ever escalating competition between airlines, a survey by international finance company Morgan Stanley shows, ranking SAS very low when it comes to competitiveness.
